definition: A thing the domain keeps track of over time, with an identity of its own (e.g. Customer, Order).
Something that happens at a point in time and is recorded (e.g. Order placed, Subscription cancelled).
A property describing a single entity or event, with no identity of its own (e.g. Customer region, Order amount).

A quantity computed by aggregating over many instances of entities or events, to assess something (e.g. Retention rate, Average order value). A numeric property of a single instance is an attribute, not a metric.
Source is a subtype of target: every instance of the source is an instance of the target. Acyclic and transitive.
Source is a component of target and makes no sense without it.
Source attribute describes instances of the target.
Symmetric catch-all for a connection nobody has named precisely yet. Allowed, but each use is an invitation to name the relationship.
The source metric is computed from instances of the target and summarises some aspect of them.
The source order or ordering event was initiated by the target customer, who is responsible for paying for it.
